$comment: Regression thresholds for the performance CI job (#867).
Tune these here rather than in the workflow so a threshold change is a
reviewable one-line diff.
thresholdPercent  — relative slowdown that counts as a regression.
absoluteFloorMs   — a change must also exceed this many milliseconds.
Without it, a 0.02ms -> 0.03ms move reads as +50%
and fails the build over nothing.
gatedMetrics      — which metrics block a merge. p50 catches a shift in
the typical case; p95 catches a fattened tail. p99 is
measured and reported but not gated, because on a
shared runner it is dominated by scheduler noise.
maxBaselineRsd    — if the baseline's own run-to-run spread exceeded this,
the scenario is reported but not gated. A benchmark
that noisy cannot support a 10% verdict, and gating on
it would train reviewers to ignore the job.
Set to 1.5 rather than something tighter on purpose.
Individual samples of a sub-millisecond operation are
dominated by GC and OS scheduling, so a high standard
deviation is normal even when p50 and p95 are stable
run to run — those percentiles are what we gate on, and
they are far more robust than the spread suggests. A
tighter limit here silently ungates most of the suite
and turns the job into decoration. Scenarios that are
genuinely unusable sit well above this.
noiseMultiplier   — reserved for per-scenario noise scaling.
